Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

Every 6 months PMP will be revised by the project management core team and each procedure will be revised by the respective department head whenever is required. 4.2 List of documents to be controlled A list of key project documents to be controlled throughout the project lifecycle (Refer 7.1). ML-P0-1000-PM-Z-ZZZ-J-PRC-204 Page 2 of 18 4.3 Document Control System (DCS) - PMWeb The Document Control System is used to number, register and control the flow and storage of all programme documentation. The input of project documentation onto the document control system is the responsibility of the Document Control department. All members of the project team needs to ensure that all documents are formally recorded through the Document Control department, as this will enable the team to have a true record and history of all project documentation and drawings that have been worked upon and distributed on the project. PMWeb is used as the Document Control System that will be managed by the PMIS Manager in PMC. 4.4 Registers Various registers and reports can be produced fromthe document control system. The project team must liaise with the Document Control

  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.

  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).

1. ALL PIPE DIAMETERS ARE IN MILLIMETER WHILE ALL OTHER DIMENSION ARE IN METER UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED. 2. PIPE DIAMETER LESS THAN 300MM ARE HDPE PIPES (PN16) WITH SDR -11 PE-100 AND DIAMETER EQUAL TO AND GREATER THAN Ø300 DUCTILE IRON PIPES CLASS C AND OPERATING PRESSURE 24 BAR SHALL BE USED FOR WHOLE POTABLE & FIRE WATER SYSTEM. 3. GATE VALVES SHALL BE DIRECT BURIED WITH SURFACE BOXES FOR PIPE DIA LESS THAN Ø300 WHILE FOR PIPE DIAMETER EQUAL TO AND LARGER THAN Ø300 SHOULD BE IN CONCRETE CHAMBERS. BUTTERFLY VALVES SHALL BE INSTALLED INSIDE CONCRETE CHAMBERS FOR PIPE DIA EQUAL TO AND MORE THAN Ø300. 4. POTABLE & FIRE WATER LINE SHALL BE INSTALLED WITH A SOIL COVER DEPTH OF 1.2M UNDER MAJOR ROADS AND 1.0M UNDER LOCAL ROADS. 5. A HORIZONTAL SEPARATION OF 3 METERS AND A VERTICAL SEPARATION OF 0.50 METER SHALL BE MAINTAINED BETWEEN POTABLE WATER AND SEWER LINES WITH THE SEWER LINE BELOW THE WATER LINE. A HORIZONTAL SEPARATION OF MINIMUM 3.00 METERS SHALL BE MAINTAINED WHERE A MINIMUM OF 0.50 METER VERTICAL SEPARATION CANNOT BE ACHIEVED. AT CROSS OVERS, WHERE THE VERTICAL SEPARATION CANNOT BE MAINTAINED WITH WATER LINE, THE SEWER LINE SHALL BE ENCASED IN CONCRETE FOR A MINIMUM LENGTH OF 3.00 METERS ON EACH SIDE OF THE WATER LINE. 6. CONCRETE THRUST BLOCKS SHALL BE PROVIDED AT ALL PIPE BENDS, TEES, REDUCERS AND INCASE OF CHANGE IN DIRECTION BOTH HORIZONTAL AND VERTICAL FOR DUCTILE IRON PIPES. FOR HDPE COMPLY WITH SUPPLIER RECOMMENDATIONS, THRUST BLOCK WILL NOT BE REQUIRED FOR HDPE PIPE IF FUSION WELDED. 7. PIPES HAVING COVER LESS THAN 1.0M SHALL BE ENCASED IN PLAIN CONCRETE. 8. ALL SERVICE CONNECTION PIPES SHALL BE INSTALLED AT DEPTH 0.80 TO 1.0 METER FROM FINISHED GRADE LEVEL. 9. FOR EXACT LOCATION OF POTABLE & FIRE WATER PIPE LINE REFER TO TYPICAL UTILITIES COORDINATION CROSS SECTIONS DRAWINGS. 10.AIR VALVES TO BE INSTALLED AT THE HIGHEST POINTS OF THE PIPES PROFILES. POTABLE WATER & FIRE FIGHTING NETWORK - GENERAL NOTES 11. FOR EXACT LOCATION OF FIRE HYDRANT TO BE COORDINATED WITH ENTRANCE (VILLA), TREES, OTHER STREET SPACE AND CIVIL DEFENCE. 12. FIRE HYDRANTS ARE PLACED AT INTERVAL OF 150M IN RESIDENTIAL AREA AND 90M IN COMMERCIAL AND HIGH-RISK AREAS AS PER NFPA / CIVIL DEFENCE/ MEWA GUIDELINES AND 75M IN ICONIC AREAS. 13. ALL PIPE DIAMETERS ARE NOMINAL PIPE SIZES,FOR HDPE, IT IS OUTSIDE AND FOR DUCTILE IRON IT IS INSIDE.. 14. CONTRACTOR IS RESPONSIBLE TO VERIFY THE GROUND LEVELS. THE TOP OF CHAMBERS SHALL BE FLUSH WITH THE ASPHALT PAVEMENT OR WITH FINISHED SIDEWALK LEVELS IN PAVED STREETS AND IN UNPAVED AREAS AS SOWN ON PLAN. 15. IN CASE OF ANY DAMAGE TO ANY PROPERTY OR UTILITY DURING CONSTRUCTION OF THIS PROJECT. CONTRACTOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE TO RE-CONSTRUCT AND RECOVER THE PROPERTY OR UTILITY TO ITS ORIGINAL FORM ON HIS OWN COST. 16. IN CASE OF ANY CLASHES BETWEEN UTILITIES, THE CONTRACTOR MUST ACHIEVE 500MM OF CLEARANCE ON THE VERTICAL POSITION OF THE UTILITIES.IN CREATING SEPARATION OF THE UTILITIES, WATER PIPE SHOULD BE ABOVE IRRIGATION PIPE.

- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

# Excavations & Trenching — Site Safety Criteria (OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P) REAL, sourced excavation and trenching thresholds for construction sites. Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.651 and 1926.652 (Subpart P) plus Appendix B, US federal regulation, public domain. US-reference standard: in Saudi Arabia site HSE is governed by Saudi labour law (MHRSD) and the project HSE plan, not OSHA, but Saudi practice broadly aligns. Note that Gulf ground conditions (sabkha, collapsible and high-water-table soils) often demand stricter shoring than the generic soil types below — always defer to the project geotechnical report. Values are metric-led (SI) with the original US-customary figure in parentheses. ## Access, egress and edge protection## Access, egress and edge protection | Requirement | Value (SI) | Original (US) | |---|---|---| | Depth at which egress (ladder/ramp/stairway) is required | 1.22 m | 4 ft | | Maximum lateral travel to egress in a trench | 7.62 m | 25 ft | | Minimum distance to keep spoil/materials from the edge | 0.61 m | 2 ft |Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.651(c)(2), (j)(2). ## When a protective system is required## When a protective system is required | Requirement | Value (SI) | Original (US) | |---|---|---| | Depth requiring a protective system (unless in stable rock) | 1.52 m | 5 ft | | Depth above which the system must be designed by a registered engineer | 6.09 m | 20 ft |Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.652(a), (b); Appendix B to Subpart P. Below 1.52 m a competent person may exempt an excavation only if examination shows no cave-in potential. ## Maximum allowable slopes by soil type (simple slope)## Maximum allowable slopes by soil type (simple slope) | Soil type | Max slope (H:V) | Angle from horizontal | |---|---|---| | Stable rock | Vertical | 90° | | Type A | 3/4 : 1 | 53° | | Type B | 1 : 1 | 45° | | Type C | 1½ : 1 | 34° |Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P, Appendix B, Table B-1. Slopes are for excavations up to 6.09 m (20 ft) deep; deeper cuts must be engineer-designed. Soil type is set by a competent person; where types are uncertain, use the more conservative (Type C). ## Inspection and water - A competent person must inspect the excavation, adjacent areas, and protective systems before each shift, as needed through the shift, and after every rainstorm or other hazard-increasing event.y rainstorm or other hazard-increasing event. - Work is not permitted in an excavation with accumulated water unless adequate precautions (support/shielding, water removal and monitoring, safety harness and lifeline) are taken. Source: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.651(h), (k). ## KSA applicability OSHA 1926 is a US-reference standard, not the governing authority in Saudi Arabia (site HSE is under Saudi labour law / MHRSD and the project HSE plan).di labour law / MHRSD and the project HSE plan). Gulf soils frequently require stricter measures than the generic Type A/B/C model — sabkha, running sand, and high water tables can make even shallow trenches hazardous. The

  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

Detailed Design Report Package 1 IP-INF-054-0000-JCB-RPT-DE-000013-A 29 Value Engineering 29.1 General As part of the DGII infrastructure design delivery process, value engineering study is an integral part of the design development process. The VE study process defines a sequence of activities that are undertaken during a VE study; before, during, and following a workshop. During the VE workshop, the VE team learns about the background issues, defines and classifies the project functions, identifies creative approaches to provide the functions, and then evaluates, develops, and presents the VE proposals to key decision makers. The VE methodology consists of seven sequential phases as depicted in Figure 29-1: below. Those are information, function analysis, evaluation, creative, develop recommendations, presentation, and finally implementation and follow-up. Each phase has its own purpose, objectives, and tasks. For example, the creative phase involves exploring the various ways to perform the function(s) identified in the function analysis phase. This allows team members to brainstorm alternatives to existing systems or methods that are in use. Brainstorming forces people to be creative and allows team members to speculate on all possible ideas to the problems presented, or alternatives to the function. Figure 29-1: Proposed Value Engineering Process for DGII Infrastructure Project Jacobs ideal proposition for DGII is to conduct VE workshop soon after completion of 60% preliminary design and cost estimates. Subsequently, the outcome of the VE workshop shall be implemented during the execution of the 60% preliminary design stage. Soon after completion of this stage and cost estimates are adjusted accordingly, a second round of VE workshop was conducted on 6th April 2023 for gauging the previous implementation and identifying plausible areas that could possibly be fine-tuned and implemented during the execution of the 90% preliminary design and for generating new VE ideas. Based on final VE session, VE initiative has been included in the Package 1 detailed design. 29.2 Value Engineering Basics by validating functionality and providing an equal or better solution without compromising the efficacy of the service or product. At present, the Value Methodology Basics followed by Jacobs for DGII VE exercise is as per SAVE International VE process. Value is defined as the ratio of function to cost and thus value can be increased by either improving the function or by reducing the cost. Value = Function / Cost The value engineering should be initiated as early as possible in the project life cycle. If value engineering becomes rework or causes project delays, it is no longer beneficial to the project. The below graph shows when value engineering moves from presenting a financial gain to a financial loss. The lower down the project cycle we implement value engineering, it may become counterproductive to the overall project budget. Design rules:

- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.
