  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).

  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).

  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.

  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

Design rules:

- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.

  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.

- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.

  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.

# CESMM4 Classification Reference Guide ## What CESMM4 Is CESMM4 is the Civil Engineering Standard Method of Measurement, 4th edition — the UK / international convention for classifying construction quantities in Bills of Quantities (BOQs). It groups items by category so that quantities can be measured and priced consistently. ## CESMM4 References Are Classifications, Not Line Items The core principle that drives every BOQ rate lookup:e principle that drives every BOQ rate lookup: > A CESMM4 reference code (e.g. `D999.46`) is a **classification reference**, not a priced line item. Rates attach to specific **described items** under each classification — diameter, depth, material, condition — not to the classification code itself. This means you cannot ask "what is the rate for D999.14?" and expect a single number. D999.14 is a category. The rate depends on the specific item described under that category.e specific item described under that category. ### Why This Matters Treating a CESMM4 code as a line item leads to fabricated rates. The correct mental model: - CESMM4 code = category header - Described item = specific quantity (e.g. "300mm HDPE culvert at 1-1.5m depth") - Rate = SAR/m attached to the described item ## How To Look Up a Rate 1. Identify the specific item description: diameter, material, depth band, condition.tion: diameter, material, depth band, condition. 2. Find that description within the CESMM4 classification group in the BOQ. 3. Read the rate against the description. Never use the CESMM4 code alone as a cost lookup key. ## Reference Infrastructure BOQ — D999.x Family The D999.x series in the reference KSA infrastructure BOQ covers stormwater, drainage, and pipeline protection works. In the preparation of the Conditions of Contract to be included in the tender documents for a contract, the following text can be used: The Conditions of Contract comprise the "General Conditions", which form part of the "Conditions of Contract for Construction" First Edition 1999 published by the Fédération Internationale des Ingénieurs-Conseils (FIDIC), and the following "Particular Conditions", which include amendments and additions to such General Conditions. There are no Sub-Clauses in the General Conditions which require data to be included in the Particular Conditions. As noted in sub-paragraph (ii) of the Foreword, the General Conditions refer to any necessary data being contained in the Appendix to Tender or (for technical matters) in the Specification. FIDIC has published a document entitled "Tendering Procedure" which presents a systematic approach to the selection of tenderers and the obtaining and evaluation of tenders; the second edition was published in 1994. The document is intended to assist the Employer to receive sound competitive tenders with a minimum of qualifications. FIDIC intends to update Tendering Procedure and to publish a guide to the use of these Conditions of Contract for Construction. Notes on the Preparation of Tender Documents The tender documents should be prepared by suitably-qualified engineers who are familiar with the technical aspects of the required works, and a review by suitably-qualified lawyers may be advisable. The tender documents issued to tenderers will consist of the Conditions of Contract, the Specification, the Drawings, and the Letter of Tender and Schedules for completion by the Tenderer. For this type of contract, where the Works are valued by measurement, the Bill of Quantities will usually be the most important Schedule. A Daywork Schedule may also be necessary, to cover minor works to be evaluated at cost. In addition, each of the Tenderers should receive the data referred to in Sub-Clause 4.10, and the Instructions to Tenderers to advise them of any special matters which the Employer wishes them to take into account when pricing the Bill of Quantities but which are not to form part of the Contract. Design rules:

- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

For example three levels of detail could be shown as follows: Table 6.1 of detail could be shown as follows: Table 6.1 2.5 When assigning new codes to the WBS, choose a code that is unique to that level and define a code that represents the type of work being described in the WBS. 3.0 WORK BREAKDOWN STRUCTURE CHARACTERISTICS 3.1 Level 1: Phase 1 is comprised of six separate projects, each coded uniquely, and therefore level 1 has been coded as follows: 4001 MotionGate; 4003 Bollywood Park; 6009 Resortwide 4005 Legoland; 4007 Park; 6009 Resortwide 4005 Legoland; 4007 Riverland (formerly River Park,RD&E); 4008 Lapita (formerly Hotel 1) 3.2 Level 2: Each Project decomposes to represent the packages that are included in the respective projects. The package names and/or numbers are established by the Contracts & Procurement team. The WBS uses the following sample 3 digit numbering system: 000 Package 0 – Project Management (Not Specific Package) 001 Package 1 – Lead Design Consultant 002 ) 001 Package 1 – Lead Design Consultant 002 Package 2 – In-Park Infrastructure Construction 003 Package 3 – Foundation Package Programme Management Manual ML-P0-1000-PM-Z-ZZ-J-MNL-206 Page 2 004 Package 4 – Main Package, etc. 3.3 Level 3: Each package is then decomposed to the following phases as applicable: PM Project Management PR Procurement DE Design EN Engineering CO Construction (of facilities where applicable); IN nstruction (of facilities where applicable); IN Installation (of rides and attractions where applicable); TC Testing & Commissioning; CL Closeout; 3.4 Level 4: Level 4 to include each area/attraction within the package as applicable. 3.5 Level 5: Level 5 is a two digit code to indicate the disciplines as applicable for each of the phase as indicated below: Level 3 (stage) Level 5 (Code) Description PM IF Interface Milestones MS Key Milestones OT Others PR CS

- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.

- VO/CO

- change request

  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).

- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.

- payment application

- payment certificate

- BOQ

  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes

  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR

  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request

  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.

  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

NON-CONFORMANCE REPORT (NCR) BÁO CÁO KHÔNG PHÙ HỢP GUIDANCE ON FORM USE An NCR can be initiated by any project team member upon observation. The observation is to be communicated to the PM/CS who will assess the observation and determine if an NCR is warranted, The PM/CS will complete part 1 of the NCR clearly detailing: - details of the observation - Variation from the specification / drawings - Identify if the NCR is related to a process or material/ product. (Analytics) The NCR will be issued to the Contractor responsible. The Contractor will review the NCR and issue a (1st) response within 3 days by completing Part 2 of the form. The response will include as a mimimun: - Details of proposed remedial action. - Calculations if required. - Brief / detailed Method statement for the remedial works. - details of specific materials to be used. DO not use MAR for this step. - Analytics - Declare: Replace, Repair, Use as is. - Analytics - 5 M root cause. - An NCR should be closed within 28days. If this is no achieveable the contractor should set a target date. The PM/CS will review that proposed rectifcation works. The PMCS may request a review by Design if considered appropriate. The PM/CS will return his review code to the Contractor using art 3 of the form. - Review Code A: Contractor can proceed with the recrification works. - Review Code B: The proposed rectification work are acceptable in principle but additonal information required. - Revoew Code C: Not approved. Contractor to look at alternative methods. The contractor will continue to submit/resubmit the proposed rectification works thought 2nd, 3rd, 4th .. response until Review Status A is received, Upon Receipt of Status A, the Contractor will execute the rectification works. Once the recification works are completed, the contractor will call for a works inspection (WIR) to have the works accepted. Once the WIR is accepted by the PMCS, The NCR will be closed and signed off by: - Contractor - QAQC - MRH Rep. (PD/PM) The NCR Register will be updated accordling. 1. ALL DIMENSIONS ARE IN MILLIMETERS AND LEVELS IN METERS. 2. CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE HVAC DETAIL DESIGN DRAWINGS FOR ALL ROOMS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE SAUDI BUILDING CODE. 3. THE LIFTING EQUIPMENT SHALL BE FINALIZED BASED ON THE WEIGHT OF HEAVIEST EQUIPMENT INSIDE THE PUMP ROOM. 4. THE SIZE, LOCATION AND DETAILS OF THE SURGE VESSELS SHALL BE VERIFIED BY THE CONTRACTOR IN THE DETAILED DESIGN STAGE. 5. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL VALIDATE THE PUMP HEAD OF THE PUMPS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE FINAL ARRANGEMENTS OF PIPE, FITTINGS AND NETWORK. 6. CONTRACTOR SHALL DESIGN THE FIRE FIGHTING SYSTEM IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE SAUDI BUILDING CODE. 7. ROCKER PIPES TO BE PROVIDED IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT TO ALL STRUCTURE FACES WHERE BURIED PIPELINE PASSES THROUGH THE STRUCTURE. 8. CONTRACTOR SHALL VERIFY THE MINIMUM SUMP WATER LEVEL IN CONSULTATION WITH THE PUMP MANUFACTURER. 9. A MINIMUM 250MM OR LENGTH OF BOLT SHALL BE MAINTAINED BETWEEN THE FLANGE AND THE WALL. 10. ALL PIPE WORK SHALL BE PN16 RATED UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED AND SHALL BE INTERNALLY & EXTERNALLY COATED WITH FUSION BONDED EPOXY TO THE APPROVAL OF THE ENGINEER. 11. VENT PIPES WITH NON-RETURN VALVES SHALL BE PROVIDED FOR SCREEN CHAMBER, WET WELL AND VALVE CHAMBERS. 12. DISMANTLING JOINTS ARE PROVIDED FOR FLEXIBILITY AND REMOVAL OF PIPES AND FITTINGS. WHERE FLANGE ADAPTORS PROPOSED, FLANGES SHALL BE SUITABLY TIED WITH THE NEAREST TIE FLANGE ON THE PIPE. THE ADJACENT PIPE SHALL BE PROVIDED WITH TIE FLANGE. 13. TIE IN CONNECTIONS TO OUTSIDE PIPEWORK (TILL 1 METER FROM THE BOUNDARY OF THE PUMPING STATION) SHALL BE OF PUMPING STATION CONTRACTOR'S SCOPE. THE DIAMETER AND MATERIAL SHALL BE CO-ORDINATED ACCURATELY WITH THE NETWORK OUTSIDE. 14. SUPPORT DETAILS FOR ALL EQUIPMENT INCLUDING PUMPS & VESSELS SHALL BE CONFIRMED BY THE CONTRACTOR/MANUFACTURER. 15. ADEQUATE SUPPORTS SHALL BE PROVIDED FOR ALL THE ABOVE GROUND PIPING. 16. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DEVELOP OUTLINE STRUCTURAL AND ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN AND SUBMIT AS PART OF THEIR TENDER DESIGN. 17. THE CONTRACTOR IS ENTIRELY RESPONSIBLE FOR THE FOLLOWING; A. ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN IN COORDINATION WITH THE CLIENT. B. STRUCTURAL DESIGN AND STRUCTURAL BASIS OF DESIGN CRITERIA. C. SITE DRAINAGE STRATEGY. D. FIRE AND LIFE SAFETY STRATEGY AND DESIGN. E. MECHANICAL AND ELECTRICAL BUILDING SERVICES DESIGN. F. AUTHORITY APPROVALS. G. CONNECTIVITY WITH THE EXTERNAL WET UTILITIES AND DRY UTILITIES NETWORKS. H. CONNECTIVITY WITH THE ROADS. I. SITE GEOTECHNICAL INVESTIGATION AND TOPOGRAPHIC SURVEY. 18. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INSTALL ALL FUTURE PIPEWORK SUCH AS PIPES WITH PUDDLE FLANGES, SO THAT NO DEMOLITION OF CIVIL WORK IS REQUIRED IN FUTURE. 19. PORTABLE LIFTING DAVIT SHALL BE PROVIDED FOR EACH LIFTING STATION WITH SOCKETS PROPOSED AT ALL LOCATIONS TO LIFT THE PUMPS AND VALVES. 20. ACTIVATED CARBON FILTERS SHALL BE PROVIDED FOR SMALL LIFTING STATIONS. FOR LARGER LIFT STATIONS BIOTRICKLING FILTER WITH ACTIVATED CARBON POLISHING SHALL BE PROVIDED, WHERE THE DESIGN SHALL BE IN CONSULTATION WITH ODOR CONTROL SYSTEM MANUFACTURER. 21. INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR SURFACES OF PUMPING STATION TO BE LINED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE SPECIFICATION. 22. PUMP STOOL SUPPORT DETAILS TO BE CONFIRMEDBY THE CONTRACTOR TO THE APPROVAL OF THE ENGINEER FOLLOWING PUMP SELECTION. 23.

14.5 Plant and Materials intended for the Works The Statement shall include the following items, as applicable, which shall be expressed in the various currencies in which the Contract Price is payable, in the sequence listed: (a) the estimated contract value of the Works executed and the Contractor’s Documents produced up to the end of the month (including Variations but excluding items described in sub-paragraphs (b) to (g) below); (b) any amounts to be added and deducted for changes in legislation and changes in cost, in accordance with Sub-Clause 13.7 [Adjustments for Changes in Legislation] and Sub-Clause 13.8 [Adjustments for Changes in Cost]; (c) any amount to be deducted for retention, calculated by applying the percentage of retention stated in the Appendix to Tender to the total of the above amounts, until the amount so retained by the Employer reaches the limit of Retention Money (if any) stated in the Appendix to Tender; (d) any amounts to be added and deducted for the advance payment and repayments in accordance with Sub-Clause 14.2 [Advance Payment]; (e) any amounts to be added and deducted for Plant and Materials in accordance with Sub-Clause 14.5 [Plant and Materials intended for the Works]; (f) any other additions or deductions which may have become due under the Contract or otherwise, including those under Clause 20 [Claims, Disputes and Arbitration]; and (g) the deduction of amounts certified in all previous Payment Certificates. If the Contract includes a schedule of payments specifying the instalments in which the Contract Price will be paid, then unless otherwise stated in this schedule: (a) the instalments quoted in this schedule of payments shall be the estimated contract values for the purposes of sub-paragraph (a) of Sub-Clause 14.3 [Application for Interim Payment Certificates]; (b) Sub-Clause 14.5 [Plant and Materials intended for the Works] shall not apply; and (c) if these instalments are not defined by reference to the actual progress achieved in executing the Works, and if actual progress is found to be less than that on which this schedule of payments was based, then the Engineer may proceed in accordance with Sub-Clause 3.5 [Determinations] to agree or determine revised instalments, which shall take account of the extent to which progress is less than that on which the instalments were previously based. If the Contract does not include a schedule of payments, the Contractor shall submit non-binding estimates of the payments which he expects to become due during each quarterly period. The first estimate shall be submitted within 42 days after the Commencement Date. Revised estimates shall be submitted at quarterly intervals, until the Taking-Over Certificate has been issued for the Works. If this Sub-Clause applies, Interim Payment Certificates shall include, under sub- paragraph (e) of Sub-Clause 14.3, (i) an amount for Plant and Materials which have been sent to the Site for incorporation in the Permanent Works, and (ii) a reduction when the contract value of such Plant and Materials is included as part of the Permanent Works under sub-paragraph (a) of Sub-Clause 14.3 [Application for Interim Payment Certificates].
