Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

3.5 Determinations The Contractor shall design (to the extent specified in the Contract), execute and complete the Works in accordance with the Contract and with the Engineer’s instructions, and shall remedy any defects in the Works. The Contractor shall provide the Plant and Contractor’s Documents specified in the Contract, and all Contractor’s Personnel, Goods, consumables and other things and services, whether of a temporary or permanent nature, required in and for this design, execution, completion and remedying of defects. The Contractor shall be responsible for the adequacy, stability and safety of all Site operations and of all methods of construction. Except to the extent specified in the Contract, the Contractor (i) shall be responsible for all Contractor’s Documents, Temporary Works, and such design of each item of Plant and Materials as is required for the item to be in accordance with the Contract, and (ii) shall not otherwise be responsible for the design or specification of the Permanent Works. Statement of Problem Urban infrastructures are becoming more complex last century. The importance of pipe detecting and the value of its application. Before excavation for maintenance of underground piping, it is necessary to understand the various site problems on topography and surface materials (e.g. position (depth and displacement) and size of other piping, as well as manholes); In order to prevent third party companies from possible damages to infrastructural equipments and people, severe damage will be generated from mistaken excavation of other piping. The severity might even affect the corporate image and living resources such as electricity, telecommunication and hydrology. Detection of underground pipeline and cable locations is very important, in addition, locations and positions of infrastructural elements with respect to each other must be known for the new infrastructural projects and for the process of operation and replacement of current infrastructure. 1.1. Introduction Developing Technologies are rapidly, so there are a lot of devices for the detection of pipeline and cable locations. These devices are working with two methods in general. One of them is electromagnetic detection method with electromagnetic induction, and the other is GPR (Ground Penetrating Radar) method working with the principle of determining the underground structure and underground holes. Especially with the new instruments and computer algorithms developed in the last years, the locations of infrastructural elements with respect to each other are determined more accurately. Ground penetrating radar (GPR) is a geophysical method that uses radar pulses to image the subsurface. This non-destructive method uses electromagnetic (EM) radiation in the microwave band (UHF/VHF frequencies) of the radio spectrum, and detects the reflected signals from subsurface structures. One of the most useful applications of GPR in urban infrastructural engineering is mapping and detection of buried pipes. This unique application becomes imperative due to the ever-growing urbanization in both developed and developing nations with its attendant demand for buried utilities. The construction, development and management of subsurface infrastructures has become a very viable business that attracts the attention of scientists and engineers over the past few years. Various utilities such as telecommunication and electric power cables, water and gas supply cables etc. are delivered through underground pipes of various sized buried at different depths. In many cases, maintenance of these infrastructures requires digging operation which leads to unintentional damage to some of the facilities. Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

security for a sum equivalent to the reasonable expenses to be incurred by the Member. No account shall be taken of any other payments due or paid to the Member. The Member shall be paid as follows, in the currency named in the Dispute Adjudication Agreement: (a) a retainer fee per calendar month, which shall be considered as payment in full for: (i) being available on 28 days' notice for all site visits and hearings; (ii) becoming and remaining conversant with all project developments and maintaining relevant files; (iii) all office and overhead expenses including secretarial services, photocopying and office supplies incurred in connection with his duties; and (iv) all services performed hereunder except those referred to in sub- paragraphs (b) and (c) of this Clause. The retainer fee shall be paid with effect from the last day of the calendar month in which the Dispute Adjudication Agreement becomes effective; until the last day of the calendar month in which the Taking-Over Certificate is issued for the whole of the Works. With effect from the first day of the calendar month following the month in which Taking-Over Certificate is issued for the whole of the Works, the retainer fee shall be reduced by 50%. This reduced fee shall be paid until the first day of the calendar month in which the Member resigns or the Dispute Adjudication Agreement is otherwise terminated. (b) a daily fee which shall be considered as payment in full for: (i) each day or part of a day up to a maximum of two days' travel time in each direction for the journey between the Member's home and the site, or another location of a meeting with the Other Members (if any); (ii) each working day on site visits, hearings or preparing decisions; and (iii) each day spent reading submissions in preparation for a hearing. (c) all reasonable expenses incurred in connection with the Member's duties, including the cost of telephone calls, courier charges, faxes and telexes, travel expenses, hotel and subsistence costs: a receipt shall be required for each item in excess of five percent of the daily fee referred to in sub-paragraph (b) of this Clause; (d) any taxes properly levied in the Country on payments made to the Member (unless a national or permanent resident of the Country) under this Clause 6. The retainer and daily fees shall be as specified in the Dispute Adjudication Agreement. Unless it specifies otherwise, these fees shall remain fixed for the first 24 calendar months, and shall thereafter be adjusted by agreement between the Employer, the Contractor and the Member, at each anniversary of the date on which the Dispute Adjudication Agreement became effective. - payment application

- payment certificate

- drawing

AL Ain Zoo – Early Works Interim Extension of Time Claim No. 07 Page 9 of 345 1.0. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 1.1. PREFACE 1.1.1 MIRAL LLC (referred to as the “Employer”) awarded M4 Contracting S.A.R.L (referred to as the “Contractor”) entered into a Contract on 01 May 2024 for the Project “AL Ain ZOO Early Works in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi – Al Ain, United Arab Emirates”, with the Works to be completed by 28 January 2025. 1.1.2 The Employer assigned Ellis Don Construction Inc. Abu Dhabi as (“the Project Management Consultant” [PMC]) in the Contract. 1.1.3 During the course of the works, the Contractor has been prevented from completing the works within the Contract time for completion by the delay events which is described in this extension of time claim submission. 1.1.4 The purpose of this submission is to set out and justify the Contractor’s entitlement to an extension of the time for completion as a result of the delay event caused by the Employer pursuant to the terms and conditions of the Contract. 1.1.5 This submission is the Contractor’s extension of time claim pursuant to Sub Clause 8.4, and Sub Clause 13.1, of the Conditions of Contract and it considers all events up to 24 October 2025. 1.1.6 The Contractor’s entitlement to an extension for the time for completion has been assessed utilizing the time impact analysis technique (Window Method) and provides evidence that an extension of time should be awarded in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Contract because of the delay event described in this interim claim submission. 1.1.7 The fundamental basis of this claim is that the Contractor has faced disruption to the schedule and planned / sequenced works and delays to the Contract completion date because of delays that are entirely a result of matters which are outside the Contractor’s control. 1.1.8 For the avoidance of doubt, this submission sets out the Contractor’s assessment of its entitlement arising out of issues, matters, and delay events addressed herein only. The Contractor reserves its right to make further AL Ain Zoo – Early Works Interim Extension of Time Claim No. 07 Page 10 of 345 assessments and submissions with respect to all other
claim

Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

You assign one document-type label from the document text only.
Choose exactly one label from the list, or unsure when the text does not support one label.
The list is the only label set. Do not add a label.
Use only the document text in the next message.
Do not use a filename, a folder, a document id, or a project name. They are not provided.
Reply with one JSON object and no other text:
{"label": "<one list entry or unsure>", "reason": "<one line>", "confidence": <your confidence, a number between 0 and 1>}
Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

15.5 Employer’s Entitlement to Termination The Employer’s election to terminate the Contract shall not prejudice any other rights of the Employer, under the Contract or otherwise. The Contractor shall then leave the Site and deliver any required Goods, all Contractor’s Documents, and other design documents made by or for him, to the Engineer. However, the Contractor shall use his best efforts to comply immediately with any reasonable instructions included in the notice (i) for the assignment of any subcontract, and (ii) for the protection of life or property or for the safety of the Works. After termination, the Employer may complete the Works and/or arrange for any other entities to do so. The Employer and these entities may then use any Goods, Contractor’s Documents and other design documents made by or on behalf of the Contractor. The Employer shall then give notice that the Contractor’s Equipment and Temporary Works will be released to the Contractor at or near the Site. The Contractor shall promptly arrange their removal, at the risk and cost of the Contractor. However, if by this time the Contractor has failed to make a payment due to the Employer, these items may be sold by the Employer in order to recover this payment. Any balance of the proceeds shall then be paid to the Contractor. As soon as practicable after a notice of termination under Sub-Clause 15.2 [Termination by Employer] has taken effect, the Engineer shall proceed in accordance with Sub-Clause 3.5 [Determinations] to agree or determine the value of the Works, Goods and Contractor’s Documents, and any other sums due to the Contractor for work executed in accordance with the Contract. After a notice of termination under Sub-Clause 15.2 [Termination by Employer] has taken effect, the Employer may: (a) proceed in accordance with Sub-Clause 2.5 [Employer’s Claims], (b) withhold further payments to the Contractor until the costs of execution, completion and remedying of any defects, damages for delay in completion (if any), and all other costs incurred by the Employer, have been established, and/or (c) recover from the Contractor any losses and damages incurred by the Employer and any extra costs of completing the Works, after allowing for any sum due to the Contractor under Sub-Clause 15.3 [Valuation at Date of Termination]. After recovering any such losses, damages and extra costs, the Employer shall pay any balance to the Contractor. The Employer shall be entitled to terminate the Contract, at any time for the Employer’s convenience, by giving notice of such termination to the Contractor. The termination shall take effect 28 days after the later of the dates on which the Contractor receives this notice or the Employer returns the Performance Security. The Employer shall not terminate the Contract under this Sub-Clause in order to execute the Works himself or to arrange for the Works to be executed by another contractor. - Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

Introduction Developing Technologies are rapidly, so there are a lot of devices for the detection of pipeline and cable locations. These devices are working with two methods in general. Especially with the new instruments and computer algorithms developed in the last years, the locations of infrastructural elements with respect to each other are determined more accurately. Ground penetrating radar (GPR) is a geophysical method that uses radar pulses to image the subsurface. - submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).

- change request

- claim

- payment application

- payment certificate

- drawing

- specification

- schedule

- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.

  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.

  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.

- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).

- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.

  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.
