AECOM letter Ref MV Culvert Constructability Report Attn: Rory Poole Contract Ref: Reference 2.8.4 Design Review 2.8.5 Design Control and Co-ordination Dear Rory The Client makes reference to the consistent and poor support in relation to the MV Culvert Constructability report requested since 7th January 2025 which to date has still not been received. The client references your Service Level Agreement noting a number of key elements where the PMC have failed to provide the level of Service support required under your Contract Section 2.8.4 PMC shall review Consultants’ design documents as they are being developed to ensure that they are in accordance with Employer’s requirements, prepared in accordance with best revision control practice with sequential revision numbers/designations and revision tables; reflect site conditions, and are suitable for their intended purpose, advise and make recommendations with respect to such factors as fit for purpose, Value Engineering and constructability, suitability for local conditions; availability of materials and labour, time requirements for procurement and construction, compliance with HSE requirements, compliance with sustainability programs; and potential impact on project costs and time Section 2.8.4 (d) PMC shall ensure that Consultants assist, cooperate, meet and review with Employer, PMC, Cost Consultant (while still engaged on the Project), Contractors and other parties to participate in any cost estimates, value engineering studies or constructability studies, so as to aid in construction direction, analysis and overall economies in the Works. Section 2.8.5 (e) – Constructability PMC shall provide advice on methods of construction, time to construct, cost of construction, sequence of operations and the like in order that designs are configured to enable efficient construction and the avoidance of in-built construction problems. PMC shall subsequently provide feedback on constructability of the designs during the construction phase. The client expresses the further concern where the PMC has effectively outsourced and expedited this task as directed by the client to the CSC to undertake. There is a clear mis-understanding within your own staff of their responsibilities when this has been allowed to happen. A clear reference of your responsibility matrix within your contract expresses this key requirement as item 17 highlighted below. The Client fully expects this review to be conducted without further delay given the passage of time since the original request as wholly unacceptable. We fully expect you to align your team with their Service Responsibilities without delay and avoid mis-directing tasks within the Project Team. The Client reserves the right to claim for any losses either direct or indirect associated with the delay in respect of completing this review and assessment and the PMC shall consider this letter as notification of such. We expect the PMC to study the respective structure and revert with a complete Constructability and Cost analysis no later than 25th March 2025.

8.4 Extension of Time for Completion If the following conditions apply, namely: (a) the Contractor has diligently followed the procedures laid down by the relevant legally constituted public authorities in the Country, (b) these authorities delay or disrupt the Contractor’s work, and (c) the delay or disruption was Unforeseeable, then this delay or disruption will be considered as a cause of delay under sub- paragraph (b) of Sub-Clause 8.4 [Extension of Time for Completion]. If, at any time: (a) actual progress is too slow to complete within the Time for Completion, and/or (b) progress has fallen (or will fall) behind the current programme under Sub- Clause 8.3 [Programme], other than as a result of a cause listed in Sub-Clause 8.4 [Extension of Time for Completion], then the Engineer may instruct the Contractor to submit, under Sub- Clause 8.3 [Programme], a revised programme and supporting report describing the revised methods which the Contractor proposes to adopt in order to expedite progress and complete within the Time for Completion. Unless the Engineer notifies otherwise, the Contractor shall adopt these revised methods, which may require increases in the working hours and/or in the numbers of Contractor’s Personnel and/or Goods, at the risk and cost of the Contractor. If these revised methods cause the Employer to incur additional costs, the Contractor shall subject to Sub-Clause 2.5 [Employer’s Claims] pay these costs to the Employer, in addition to delay damages (if any) under Sub-Clause 8.7 below. If the Contractor fails to comply with Sub-Clause 8.2 [Time for Completion], the Contractor shall subject to Sub-Clause 2.5 [Employer’s Claims] pay delay damages to the Employer for this default. These delay damages shall be the sum stated in the Appendix to Tender, which shall be paid for every day which shall elapse between the relevant Time for Completion and the date stated in the Taking-Over Certificate. However, the total amount due under this Sub-Clause shall not exceed the maximum amount of delay damages (if any) stated in the Appendix to Tender. These delay damages shall be the only damages due from the Contractor for such default, other than in the event of termination under Sub-Clause 15.2 [Termination by Employer] prior to completion of the Works. These damages shall not relieve the Contractor from his obligation to complete the Works, or from any other duties, obligations or responsibilities which he may have under the Contract. The Engineer may at any time instruct the Contractor to suspend progress of part or all of the Works. During such suspension, the Contractor shall protect, store and secure such part or the Works against any deterioration, loss or damage. The Engineer may also notify the cause for the suspension. If and to the extent that the cause is notified and is the responsibility of the Contractor, the following Sub- Clauses 8.9, 8.10 and 8.11 shall not apply. 8.5 Delays Caused by Authorities 8.6 Rate of Progress 8.7 Delay Damages

20.6 Arbitration further access to the Site, and appropriate facilities, as the DAB may require for the purposes of making a decision on such dispute. The DAB shall be deemed to be not acting as arbitrator(s). Within 84 days after receiving such reference, or within such other period as may be proposed by the DAB and approved by both Parties, the DAB shall give its decision, which shall be reasoned and shall state that it is given under this Sub-Clause. The decision shall be binding on both Parties, who shall promptly give effect to it unless and until it shall be revised in an amicable settlement or an arbitral award as described below. Unless the Contract has already been abandoned, repudiated or terminated, the Contractor shall continue to proceed with the Works in accordance with the Contract. If either Party is dissatisfied with the DAB’s decision, then either Party may, within 28 days after receiving the decision, give notice to the other Party of its dissatisfaction. If the DAB fails to give its decision within the period of 84 days (or as otherwise approved) after receiving such reference, then either Party may, within 28 days after this period has expired, give notice to the other Party of its dissatisfaction. In either event, this notice of dissatisfaction shall state that it is given under this Sub- Clause, and shall set out the matter in dispute and the reason(s) for dissatisfaction. Except as stated in Sub-Clause 20.7 [Failure to Comply with Dispute Adjudication Board’s Decision] and Sub-Clause 20.8 [Expiry of Dispute Adjudication Board’s Appointment], neither Party shall be entitled to commence arbitration of a dispute unless a notice of dissatisfaction has been given in accordance with this Sub-Clause. If the DAB has given its decision as to a matter in dispute to both Parties, and no notice of dissatisfaction has been given by either Party within 28 days after it received the DAB’s decision, then the decision shall become final and binding upon both Parties. Where notice of dissatisfaction has been given under Sub-Clause 20.4 above, both Parties shall attempt to settle the dispute amicably before the commencement of arbitration. However, unless both Parties agree otherwise, arbitration may be commenced on or after the fifty-sixth day after the day on which notice of dissatis- faction was given, even if no attempt at amicable settlement has been made. Unless settled amicably, any dispute in respect of which the DAB’s decision (if any) has not become final and binding shall be finally settled by international arbitration. Unless otherwise agreed by both Parties: (a) the dispute shall be finally settled under the Rules of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce, (b) the dispute shall be settled by three arbitrators appointed in accordance with these Rules, and (c) the arbitration shall be conducted in the language for communications defined in Sub-Clause 1.4 [Law and Language]. The arbitrator(s) shall have full power to open up, review and revise any certificate, determination, instruction, opinion or valuation of the Engineer, and any decision of the DAB, relevant to the dispute.

Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

# EVM Thresholds and Traffic Light System ## CPI and SPI — Definitions **CPI (Cost Performance Index)** = EV ÷ AC - CPI > 1.0 means cost efficient — earned value exceeds actual cost. - CPI = 1.0 means on budget. - CPI < 1.0 means over budget — earned value is less than actual cost. **SPI (Schedule Performance Index)** = EV ÷ PV (also expressed as BCWP ÷ BCWS) - SPI > 1.0 means ahead of schedule. - SPI = 1.0 means on schedule. - SPI < 1.0 means behind schedule.on schedule. - SPI < 1.0 means behind schedule. Interpretation note: an SPI of 0.8 means the project has earned only 80 cents of value for every dollar planned. An SPI below 1.0 always means the project is behind schedule. ## CPI Traffic Light System The CPI Traffic Light is the standard executive-dashboard rule: - **GREEN — CPI > 1.00** — Under Budget, Cost Efficient. Keep doing what works. - **AMBER — 0.90 ≤ CPI ≤ 1.00** — Slightly Over Budget. Investigate and take action.lightly Over Budget. Investigate and take action. - **RED — CPI < 0.90** — Over Budget, Cost Inefficient. Take corrective action now. The RED threshold is **CPI < 0.90**. Anything below 0.90 is RED. The AMBER band is **0.90 ≤ CPI ≤ 1.00** (inclusive on both ends). A CPI of exactly 0.90 is AMBER. A CPI of exactly 1.00 is AMBER. The GREEN band is **CPI > 1.00** (strictly greater than 1.00). ### Worked Examplestrictly greater than 1.00). ### Worked Examples - CPI of 0.85 → RED (below the 0.90 threshold). - CPI of 0.91 → AMBER (above 0.90, within the 0.90-1.00 band). - CPI of 0.93 → AMBER. - CPI of 0.95 → AMBER. - CPI of 1.05 → GREEN (above 1.00). - CPI of 0.72 → RED. Action required: forensic cost-variance analysis and a recovery plan. The project is materially overspending against earned value. ## SPI Traffic Light Systemainst earned value. ## SPI Traffic Light System - **GREEN — SPI > 1.00** — Ahead of Schedule. Maintain momentum. - **AMBER — 0.90 ≤ SPI ≤ 1.00** — Slightly Behind. Review plan and recover. - **RED — SPI < 0.90** — Behind Schedule, At Risk. Take corrective action now. ## Combined CPI / SPI Interpretation Both indices together describe project health: - CPI > 1.0 AND SPI > 1.0 → Ahead and under budget. Great performance. - CPI < 1.0 AND SPI > 1.0 → Ahead but over budget. Monitor costs.SPI > 1.0 → Ahead but over budget. Monitor costs. - CPI > 1.0 AND SPI < 1.0 → On budget but behind. Recover schedule. - CPI < 1.0 AND SPI < 1.0 → Behind and over budget. Take corrective action immediately. ## TCPI — To-Complete Performance Index TCPI = (BAC − EV) ÷ (BAC − AC) TCPI is the cost efficiency required for the remaining work to complete on budget. Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

NON-CONFORMANCE REPORT (NCR) BÁO CÁO KHÔNG PHÙ HỢP Form No./Biểu mẫu số: QMS.C.3 GUIDANCE ON FORM USE An NCR can be initiated by any project team member upon observation. The observation is to be communicated to the PM/CS who will assess the observation and determine if an NCR is warranted, The PM/CS will complete part 1 of the NCR clearly detailing: - details of the observation - Variation from the specification / drawings - Identify if the NCR is related to a process or material/ product. (Analytics) The NCR will be issued to the Contractor responsible. The Contractor will review the NCR and issue a (1st) response within 3 days by completing Part 2 of the form. The response will include as a mimimun: - Details of proposed remedial action. - Calculations if required. - Brief / detailed Method statement for the remedial works. - details of specific materials to be used. DO not use MAR for this step. - Analytics - Declare: Replace, Repair, Use as is. - Analytics - 5 M root cause. - An NCR should be closed within 28days. If this is no achieveable the contractor should set a target date. The PM/CS will review that proposed rectifcation works. The PMCS may request a review by Design if considered appropriate. The PM/CS will return his review code to the Contractor using art 3 of the form. - Review Code A: Contractor can proceed with the recrification works. - Review Code B: The proposed rectification work are acceptable in principle but additonal information required. - Revoew Code C: Not approved. Contractor to look at alternative methods. The contractor will continue to submit/resubmit the proposed rectification works thought 2nd, 3rd, 4th .. response until Review Status A is received, Upon Receipt of Status A, the Contractor will execute the rectification works. Once the recification works are completed, the contractor will call for a works inspection (WIR) to have the works accepted. Once the WIR is accepted by the PMCS, The NCR will be closed and signed off by: - Contractor - PM/CS - MRH QAQC - MRH Rep. (PD/PM) The NCR Register will be updated accordling. NOTE: Technical Submittal Form and Material Approval Request forms are not requried for submitting attachments to the NCR. The NCR updates are the communication tool. All NCR communications and updates will be compiled to one NCR file on record. Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.
