- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

2.5 Employer’s Claims The particulars shall specify the Clause or other basis of the claim, and shall include substantiation of the amount and/or extension to which the Employer considers himself to be entitled in connection with the Contract. The Engineer shall then proceed in accordance with Sub-Clause 3.5 [Determinations] to agree or determine (i) the amount (if any) which the Employer is entitled to be paid by the Contractor, and/or (ii) the extension (if any) of the Defects Notification Period in accordance with Sub- Clause 11.3 [Extension of Defects Notification Period]. This amount may be included as a deduction in the Contract Price and Payment Certificates. The Employer shall only be entitled to set off against or make any deduction from an amount certified in a Payment Certificate, or to otherwise claim against the Contractor, in accordance with this Sub-Clause. The Employer shall appoint the Engineer who shall carry out the duties assigned to him in the Contract. The Engineer’s staff shall include suitably qualified engineers and other professionals who are competent to carry out these duties. The Engineer shall have no authority to amend the Contract. The Engineer may exercise the authority attributable to the Engineer as specified in or necessarily to be implied from the Contract. If the Engineer is required to obtain the approval of the Employer before exercising a specified authority, the requirements shall be as stated in the Particular Conditions. The Employer undertakes not to impose further constraints on the Engineer’s authority, except as agreed with the Contractor. However, whenever the Engineer exercises a specified authority for which the Employer’s approval is required, then (for the purposes of the Contract) the Employer shall be deemed to have given approval. Except as otherwise stated in these Conditions: (a) whenever carrying out duties or exercising authority, specified in or implied by the Contract, the Engineer shall be deemed to act for the Employer; (b) the Engineer has no authority to relieve either Party of any duties, obligations or responsibilities under the Contract; and (c) any approval, check, certificate, consent, examination, inspection, instruction, notice, proposal, request, test, or similar act by the Engineer (including absence of disapproval) shall not relieve the Contractor from any responsibility he has under the Contract, including responsibility for errors, omissions, discrepancies and non-compliances. The Engineer may from time to time assign duties and delegate authority to assistants, and may also revoke such assignment or delegation. These assistants may include a resident engineer, and/or independent inspectors appointed to inspect and/or test items of Plant and/or Materials. The assignment, delegation or revocation shall be in writing and shall not take effect until copies have been received by both Parties. However, unless otherwise agreed by both Parties, the Engineer shall not delegate the authority to determine any matter in accordance with Sub-Clause 3.5 [Determinations]. Assistants shall be suitably qualified persons, who are competent to carry out these 3.1 Engineer’s Duties and Authority

Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.

  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.

  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

1.8 Care and Supply of Documents The Contractor shall give notice to the Engineer whenever the Works are likely to be delayed or disrupted if any necessary drawing or instruction is not issued to the Contractor within a particular time, which shall be reasonable. The notice shall include details of the necessary drawing or instruction, details of why and by when it should be issued, and details of the nature and amount of the delay or disruption likely to be suffered if it is late. If the Contractor suffers delay and/or incurs Cost as a result of a failure of the Engineer to issue the notified drawing or instruction within a time which is reasonable and is specified in the notice with supporting details, the Contractor shall give a further notice to the Engineer and shall be entitled subject to Sub-Clause 20.1 [Contractor’s Claims] to: (a) an extension of time for any such delay, if completion is or will be delayed, under Sub-Clause 8.4 [Extension of Time for Completion], and (b) payment of any such Cost plus reasonable profit, which shall be included in the Contract Price. After receiving this further notice, the Engineer shall proceed in accordance with Sub- Clause 3.5 [Determinations] to agree or determine these matters. However, if and to the extent that the Engineer’s failure was caused by any error or delay by the Contractor, including an error in, or delay in the submission of, any of the Contractor’s Documents, the Contractor shall not be entitled to such extension of time, Cost or profit. As between the Parties, the Contractor shall retain the copyright and other intellectual property rights in the Contractor’s Documents and other design documents made by (or on behalf of) the Contractor. The Contractor shall be deemed (by signing the Contract) to give to the Employer a non-terminable transferable non-exclusive royalty-free licence to copy, use and communicate the Contractor’s Documents, including making and using modifications of them. This licence shall: (a) apply throughout the actual or intended working life (whichever is longer) of the relevant parts of the Works, (b) entitle any person in proper possession of the relevant part of the Works to copy, use and communicate the Contractor’s Documents for the purposes of completing, operating, maintaining, altering, adjusting, repairing and demolishing the Works, and (c) in the case of Contractor’s Documents which are in the form of computer programs and other software, permit their use on any computer on the Site and other places as envisaged by the Contract, including replacements of any computers supplied by the Contractor. The Contractor’s Documents and other design documents made by (or on behalf of) the Contractor shall not, without the Contractor’s consent, be used, copied or communicated to a third party by (or on behalf of) the Employer for purposes other than those permitted under this Sub-Clause. As between the Parties, the Employer shall retain the copyright and other intellectual property rights in the Specification, the Drawings and other documents made by (or on behalf of) the Employer. Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

8.8 Suspension of Work If the Contractor suffers delay and/or incurs Cost from complying with the Engineer’s instructions under Sub-Clause 8.8 [Suspension of Work] and/or from resuming the work, the Contractor shall give notice to the Engineer and shall be entitled subject to Sub-Clause 20.1 [Contractor’s Claims] to: (a) an extension of time for any such delay, if completion is or will be delayed, under Sub-Clause 8.4 [Extension of Time for Completion], and (b) payment of any such Cost, which shall be included in the Contract Price. After receiving this notice, the Engineer shall proceed in accordance with Sub- Clause 3.5 [Determinations] to agree or determine these matters. The Contractor shall not be entitled to an extension of time for, or to payment of the Cost incurred in, making good the consequences of the Contractor’s faulty design, workmanship or materials, or of the Contractor’s failure to protect, store or secure in accordance with Sub-Clause 8.8 [Suspension of Work]. The Contractor shall be entitled to payment of the value (as at the date of suspension) of Plant and/or Materials which have not been delivered to Site, if: (a) the work on Plant or delivery of Plant and/or Materials has been suspended for more than 28 days, and (b) the Contractor has marked the Plant and/or Materials as the Employer’s property in accordance with the Engineer’s instructions. If the suspension under Sub-Clause 8.8 [Suspension of Work] has continued for more than 84 days, the Contractor may request the Engineer’s permission to proceed. If the Engineer does not give permission within 28 days after being requested to do so, the Contractor may, by giving notice to the Engineer, treat the suspension as an omission under Clause 13 [Variations and Adjustments] of the affected part of the Works. If the suspension affects the whole of the Works, the Contractor may give notice of termination under Sub-Clause 16.2 [Termination by Contractor]. After the permission or instruction to proceed is given, the Contractor and the Engineer shall jointly examine the Works and the Plant and Materials affected by the suspension. The Contractor shall make good any deterioration or defect in or loss of the Works or Plant or Materials, which has occurred during the suspension. The Contractor shall carry out the Tests on Completion in accordance with this Clause and Sub-Clause 7.4 [Testing], after providing the documents in accordance with sub-paragraph (d) of Sub-Clause 4.1 [Contractor’s General Obligations]. The Contractor shall give to the Engineer not less than 21 days’ notice of the date after which the Contractor will be ready to carry out each of the Tests on Completion. Unless otherwise agreed, Tests on Completion shall be carried out within 14 days after this date, on such day or days as the Engineer shall instruct. In considering the results of the Tests on Completion, the Engineer shall make 9 Tests on Completion 8.9 Consequences of Suspension 8.10 Payment for Plant and Materials in Event of Suspension 8.11 Prolonged Suspension 8.12 Resumption of Work

- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.

1.1.2.4 “Engineer” means the person appointed by the Employer to act as the Engineer for the purposes of the Contract and named in the Appendix to Tender, or other person appointed from time to time by the Employer and notified to the Contractor under Sub-Clause 3.4 [Replacement of the Engineer]. 1.1.2.5 “Contractor’s Representative” means the person named by the Contractor in the Contract or appointed from time to time by the Contractor under Sub-Clause 4.3 [Contractor’s Representative], who acts on behalf of the Contractor. 1.1.2.6 “Employer’s Personnel” means the Engineer, the assistants referred to in Sub-Clause 3.2 [Delegation by the Engineer] and all other staff, labour and other employees of the Engineer and of the Employer; and any other personnel notified to the Contractor, by the Employer or the Engineer, as Employer’s Personnel. 1.1.2.7 “Contractor’s Personnel” means the Contractor’s Representative and all personnel whom the Contractor utilises on Site, who may include the staff, labour and other employees of the Contractor and of each Subcontractor; and any other personnel assisting the Contractor in the execution of the Works. 1.1.2.8 “Subcontractor” means any person named in the Contract as a subcontractor, or any person appointed as a subcontractor, for a part of the Works; and the legal successors in title to each of these persons. 1.1.2.9 “DAB” means the person or three persons so named in the Contract, or other person(s) appointed under Sub-Clause 20.2 [Appointment of the Dispute Adjudication Board] or Sub-Clause 20.3 [Failure to Agree Dispute Adjudication Board] 1.1.2.10 “FIDIC” means the Fédération Internationale des Ingénieurs-Conseils, the international federation of consulting engineers. 1.1.3.1 “Base Date” means the date 28 days prior to the latest date for submission of the Tender. 1.1.3.2 “Commencement Date” means the date notified under Sub-Clause 8.1 [Commencement of Works]. 1.1.3.3 “Time for Completion” means the time for completing the Works or a Section (as the case may be) under Sub-Clause 8.2 [Time for Completion], as stated in the Appendix to Tender (with any extension under Sub- Clause 8.4 [Extension of Time for Completion]), calculated from the Commencement Date. 1.1.3.4 “Tests on Completion” means the tests which are specified in the Contract or agreed by both Parties or instructed as a Variation, and which are carried 1.1.2 Parties and Persons 1.1.3 Dates, Tests, Periods and Completion out under Clause 9 [Tests on Completion] before the Works or a Section (as the case may be) are taken over by the Employer. 1.1.3.5 “Taking-Over Certificate” means a certificate issued under Clause 10 [Employer’s Taking Over].

IP-INF-053-0000-JCB-DWG-SE-100-1000002 (Security, Rev A) Project: DIRIYAH GATE PHASE II Notes: - GENERAL NOTES: - 1. THE SECURITY DRAWINGS SHALL BE READ IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE TECHNICAL SECURITY REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT AND THE SECURITY EQUIPMENT TYPICAL DRAWING SET. - 2. ALL ANPR CAMERAS LOCATED NEAR ENTRANCES/HVM SHALL BE PLACED ON THE NEAREST POSSIBLE LIGHT POLES THAT STILL GRANT FULL VISIBILITY OF THE ENTRANCE. - 3. THE CCTV EQUIPMENT SHALL BE INSTALLED IN SAFE AND CLEAN LOCATION. NT SHALL BE INSTALLED IN SAFE AND CLEAN LOCATION. - 4. ALL OUTDOOR VSS EQUIPMENT MUST BE SUITABLE FOR INSTALLATION AND OPERATION IN THE PROPOSED ENVIRONMENT THROUGHOUT THE RANGE OF WEATHER CONDITIONS THAT - COULD BE REASONABLY EXPECTED. - 5. ANPR CAMERAS SHALL HAVE THE FOLLOWING INSTALLATION CONDITIONS; - - THE CAMERAS HORIZONTAL ANGLE NO MORE THAN 10 DEGREES FROM A VERTICAL LEVEL ON THE CAR PLATE AND A VERTICAL ANGLE OF NO MORE THAN 15 DEGREES UP OR A VERTICAL ANGLE OF NO MORE THAN 15 DEGREES UP OR - DOWN AND A HEIGHT OF CAMERA NO MORE THAN 2M AND NOT LESS THAN 1.6M. - -FOR ANPR CAMERAS INSTALLED ON A GANTRY, CAMERAS SHALL BE INSTALLED BETWEEN TWO LANES WITH A VERTICAL ANGLE OF NO MORE THAN 30 DEGREES FROM A - HORIZONTAL LEVEL ON THE CAR PLATE AND A HEIGHT BETWEEN 5M TO 6M IN CASES OF ROAD SPEED LESS THAN 60 KM/H. - 6. WHERE POSSIBLE ALL CAMERAS SHALL BE POSITIONED OFF LIGHT POLES. ALL CAMERAS SHALL BE POSITIONED OFF LIGHT POLES. SHOULD THE FIELD OF VIEW NOT MEET THE REQUIRED FIELD OF VIEW THEN A STANDALONE CAMERA POLE - MATCHING THE LIGHT POLES SHALL BE USED. - 7. ALL HVM BOLLARDS SHALL INTERFACE TO THE CLOSEST FIELD SECURITY CABINET VIA COPPER CABLING AND THEN BE INTERFACED TO THEIR RESPECTIVE SCCC VIA FIBER OPTIC - CABLING AS PER THE DISTRICT DESIGNATION IN THE SECURITY DESIGN REPORT. STRICT DESIGNATION IN THE SECURITY DESIGN REPORT. - 8. FIELD EQUIPMENT CABINETS (FEC) SHALL BE INSTALLED ON EACH LIGHT POLE WITH VIDEO SURVEILLANCE. - 9. FEC LAYOUTS ARE TYPICAL ONLY AS PER THE TYPICAL DRAWINGS SET. DESIGN SHALL SUIT THE CONNECTED EQUIPMENT REQUIREMENTS. - 10. THE FEC'S COMMUNICATION LINK SHALL BE OVER FIBER OPTIC CABLE (BY OTHERS). - 11. WHERE POSSIBLE, THE SYSTEM SHALL BE FED FROM LOCAL SUPPLIES, SEPARATE AND INDEPENDENT OF OTHER LOADS THAT PROVIDE EXTRA 25% OF FULL LOAD. OTHER LOADS THAT PROVIDE EXTRA 25% OF FULL LOAD. ALTERNATIVELY, - DIRIYAH GATE PHASE II - CAMERAS AND OTHER REMOTELY LOCATED EQUIPMENT SHALL BE FED FROM THE LIGHTING CIRCUIT OF THAT POLE. - & KING KHALID ROAD - 12. ALL CAMERA'S ARE TO BE FIXED CAMERAS UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED - INFRASTRUCTURE DESIGN - KINGDOM OF SAUDI ARABIA - 13. THERE SHALL BE NO MORE THAN THREE CCTV CAMERAS MOUNTED TO A POLE

Design rules:
- A label is decided from document content only. Filename, folder, source site and form number never decide a label.
- Regional names map to one label (see Regional mappings).
- "other" is only for construction project documents that fit none of the named labels.
- Letter-form notices that are a claim, RFI, NCR, site instruction or payment application take that specific label, not correspondence.
- A register lists many items of one kind; a single item listed in it takes its own label (one VO is VO/CO; the VO log is register/log).
- Change request is about the works (a scope change asked for or priced, not yet instructed); claim is about entitlement (time or money asserted with particulars). A document that directs the change is VO/CO even when the price is not agreed.
Allowed labels:
- RFI
  Definition: A formal request for information about design, specification, drawing or site condition, seeking an answer that unlocks work.
  Is not: A general email; a submittal; a claim; a response letter alone; an RFI log (that is register/log).
- submittal
  Definition: Contractor-issued package seeking approval or review of product data, shop drawings, samples or method material before use or installation.
  Is not: A drawing issued for construction; a transmittal cover with no submittal substance; an RFI; a submittal register (that is register/log).
- transmittal
  Definition: A cover sheet that records the issue or return of a specific batch of documents between parties, with issue purpose and distribution.
  Is not: The document being transmitted; a submittal package itself; meeting minutes; a running document or drawing register (that is register/log).
- VO/CO
  Definition: The change or variation instrument itself that alters scope, price and/or time.
  Is not: A memo, agenda, staff report or email that merely recommends or approves a change; a change request (a change asked for or priced but not instructed); a claim seeking a change; a programme update; a VO log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation order (VO), change order (CO), variation instruction, engineer's instruction (EI) when it varies the works, architect's instruction (AI) when it varies the works, employer's instruction or field change notice when it varies the works, construction change directive.
  A construction change directive directs the change, so it is VO/CO even when the price or time is not yet agreed.
- change request
  Definition: A request for a change to the works, or a priced proposal for one, that has not been instructed: a scope change asked for or priced.
  Is not: A variation order or construction change directive (the instrument that directs the change; that is VO/CO); a claim (an assertion of entitlement to time or money with particulars, such as an EOT letter); a variation settlement recommendation (that is report); a procedure describing how to raise a change; a log of changes (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation request, change order request (COR), potential change order (PCO), proposal request, request for modification, priced variation proposal, change control form seeking approval of a proposed change.
  Change request is about the works; claim is about entitlement. A priced variation proposal is change request; an EOT letter with particulars is claim.
- claim
  Definition: A contractor (or other party) notice or submission asserting entitlement to time and/or money under the contract, with particulars of cause and quantum or an express reservation of rights.
  Is not: Policy or guidance about claims; a change order already agreed; a change request (a priced variation proposal about the works); a routine progress report; a blank claim template; a claims register (that is register/log); a payment application.
  Regional names that map here: notice of claim, claim for extension of time (EOT claim), claim for additional payment, request for equitable adjustment (REA) when framed as a contractual claim.
- payment application
  Definition: The contractor's (or subcontractor's) application for payment stating the amount it claims is due for work done and materials, submitted for review and certification.
  Is not: The engineer's/certifier's payment certificate; a supplier invoice outside the contract payment cycle; a claim for additional entitlement; a cost report.
  Regional names that map here: application for payment, interim application, pay application / pay app, progress claim (AU/NZ), payment claim (AU/NZ security of payment), contractor's statement (FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.3).
  Combined forms (e.g. one form with both the contractor's application and the certifier's block): label by what the document as returned contains. If the certifier's section is blank or not signed, it is payment application.
- payment certificate
  Definition: The certificate issued by the engineer, architect, QS or employer's representative stating the amount certified as due to the contractor.
  Is not: The contractor's application; a change order; a cost report without a certified amount; a payment register (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: interim payment certificate (IPC), final payment certificate, certificate of payment, payment certificate, valuation certified by the QS, engineer's certificate under FIDIC Sub-Clause 14.6/14.13.
  Combined forms: if the certifier's section is completed and signed with a certified amount, it is payment certificate.
- drawing
  Definition: A design or construction drawing (plan, section, elevation, detail, shop drawing issued as a drawing) showing geometry or arrangement of the works.
  Is not: A schedule bar chart; a specification; a photograph report; a sketch inside an RFI unless the whole document is issued as a drawing; a drawing register (that is register/log).
- specification
  Definition: Prescriptive or performance text stating materials, workmanship, standards or procedures for the works (specification sections, particular specifications, employer's requirements technical clauses).
  Is not: A method statement; a contract commercial clause set; a programme.
- schedule
  Definition: A time programme for the works: baseline, updated or look-ahead programme with activities, logic, durations and dates (Gantt, CPM, P6 print, construction sequence programme).
  Is not: Narrative text about how schedules must be prepared; a meeting agenda; a list of items with status but no time network (that is register/log).
- report
  Definition: A narrative or tabulated report of status, progress, inspection findings, investigation or advice, issued for a point in time or period (progress report, site report, technical report, consultant advice report).
  Is not: Meeting minutes; an NCR; a payment certificate; a claim; a running record of many items maintained over time (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: variation settlement recommendation.
  A variation settlement recommendation is report: it recommends a valuation and does not instruct.
- correspondence
  Definition: A project letter or email between parties that is not primarily one of the named instruments above (general notice, cover letter, reply, chase, confirmation).
  Is not: An RFI; a claim notice; an NCR; a site instruction; a payment application; a change request; a variation order.
- BOQ
  Definition: Bill of quantities or schedule of rates: itemised measured work with quantities and (usually) rates or price columns used for tender or payment measurement.
  Is not: A payment certificate or application; a cost report; a material delivery note.
- contract
  Definition: The agreement or deed that forms the contract (articles of agreement, contract agreement, letter of acceptance with annexed conditions, main conditions of contract as executed).
  Is not: A variation order; a specification volume alone; meeting minutes of a commercial discussion.
- method statement
  Definition: Contractor's method statement or work method: step-by-step how a work activity will be carried out, including plant, sequence and controls.
  Is not: A specification; a risk assessment alone unless issued as the method statement; a programme.
- meeting minutes
  Definition: Record of a project meeting (kick-off, progress, technical, commercial) listing attendees, matters discussed and actions.
  Is not: A report; an agenda with no record of discussion; correspondence confirming one action; a standalone action tracker (that is register/log).
- NCR
  Definition: Non-conformance / non-compliance report: formal record that work, material or process does not meet the specified requirement, usually with disposition.
  Is not: A routine inspection checklist with no non-conformance; a site instruction; an RFI; an NCR log (that is register/log).
- inspection request
  Definition: Request for inspection or test: notice that work is ready for inspection, witness or test.
  Is not: An information RFI; an NCR; an inspection report (that is report); an inspection request log (that is register/log).
  Regional names that map here: inspection and test request (ITR), request for inspection (called "RFI" in some Gulf practice — disambiguate from information RFI by content), notice of inspection, work inspection request (WIR), material inspection request (MIR).
- site instruction
  Definition: Direction issued on site to proceed, hold, or change work methods or temporary works without (by itself) agreeing time or money. An engineer's instruction that does not vary price or time stays here; if it varies price or time it is VO/CO.
  Is not: A variation order; a method statement; meeting minutes.
  Regional names that map here: employer's instruction and field change notice when they do not vary the works; architect's supplemental instruction.
  An employer's instruction or field change notice is site instruction unless it varies the works (scope, price or time); then it is VO/CO.
- register/log
  Definition: A tabulated running record of many items of one kind, with status columns, maintained over time. The register is not the items it lists.
  Is not: A single item from the list (label that item by its own type); a BOQ (priced quantities, not a status record); a programme (time network); a one-off report table.
  Examples: VO log, change order log, change request log, submittal register, RFI log, drawing register, document register, risk register, issues log, action tracker, NCR log, claims register, payment register, stakeholder tracker, permit tracker.
- other
  Definition: A genuine construction project document that does not fit any named label above (for example: insurance certificate, permit/NOC, survey certificate, test certificate, warranty, handover certificate).
  Is not: A way to park a document you have not read; a template with no project content.
